messages:
incident-bot: Paging: Canary rollout v1.4.0 to prod-apac is causing a measurable p99 increase on /stream endpoints (streaming stalls + elevated tail latency). Alerting p95 ~ 450ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~ 1.2s -> 3.8s. Degraded for ~6 minutes. Auto-fallback didn't trigger. :rotating_light:

oncall-amar: acknowledged. I'm on it. grabbing traces now. which routes are affected?

sre-jordan: seeing a spike in multiplex queue depth on mux-nodes-apac-2/3, connection queueing up. Correlates with rollout timestamp.

eng-runtime-lee: rechecked canary rollout config — traffic was 10% to canary group in apac. Canary model uses new kernel selection + continuous batching tweak.

infra-tim: we also have a small deployment failure ~apac-stats agent showing high epoll wakeups on those machines. wondering if kernel change in runtime triggers different socket behavior.

support-nina: FYI we've got 2 customers with active sessions reporting repeated stalls on streaming chat (session IDs: s-2371, s-2389). Not yet widespread but they are seeing UX timeouts.

oncall-amar: priority: contain customer impact, roll traffic off canary, collect traces for root cause. Jordan/Tim, can you confirm if we can reweight traffic for prod-apac only?

sre-jordan: yes. I can reweight at the router layer. Will cut canary to 0% for apac in 60s, leaving other regions intact.

eng-runtime-lee: please hold — before we cut, can we snapshot KV-cache/kvc metrics? suspect prefix caching + different attention kernel is causing larger KV sizes -> memory pressure -> stalls. I'll grab heap/KV stats.

infra-tim: acknowledged. grabbing host-level metrics and tcp queue lengths.

incident-bot: Action: reweight request queued by sre-jordan. Command: `routerctl set-weight canary-v1.4.0 0 --region apac`.

sre-jordan: running command now. paste logs:
```
$ routerctl set-weight canary-v1.4.0 0 --region apac
OK: new weights applied (canary: 0%, stable: 100%)
```

eng-runtime-lee: saw a drop in new stalls immediately after reweight, p95 falling back toward baseline. Good. We still need full rollback plan if impact resurges.

oncall-amar: Jordan — can you also pin mux routing to avoid cross-region multiplexing for the next hour? want to reduce cross-traffic.

sre-jordan: yes. `muxctl set-policy apac local-only --duration 1h` executed.

infra-tim: host metrics: abnormal socket backlog on mux-nodes-apac-2 peaked at 18k concurrent queued events; CPU bounded by kernel context switches. There was a small kernel upgrade on that instance fleet last week (4.19 -> backport). Possibly exacerbate epoll behavior with high async timers.

eng-runtime-lee: K/V sizes: canary variant increases per-request KV by ~30% due to longer context window; combined with continuous batching it seems to push queueing window and cause head-of-line blocking for streaming.

support-nina: Ticketed customers updated: we've advised that we're rolling off the canary in apac and restoring normal service. Monitoring for recovery; will follow up with a postmortem.

product-ryan: Any visible data loss or incorrect outputs for those sessions? customers care more about stalls than subtle output diffs right now.

eng-runtime-lee: no evidence of degraded quality, mostly timeouts/stalls. model outputs appear consistent.

oncall-amar: next steps: 1) keep canary 0% in apac, 2) collect full master traces (span IDs below), 3) if stable for 10m, re-evaluate canary config (reduce batching, revert kernel selector), 4) prepare rollback v1.3.x air-gap if needed.

eng-runtime-lee: collecting traces. example trace ids: trace:ab12-ff34, trace:ab12-ff35, trace:ab12-ff36. I'll upload to traces/4309/canary-collection.

sre-jordan: p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 700ms within 90s of reweight + mux local-only. p95 back to ~220ms. Looks stable so far.

infra-tim: queue depth also decreased to baseline. kernel context switches reduced. but I recommend we keep the local-only mux policy until we confirm full cluster health.

oncall-amar: agree. set policy for 1h and we will revisit.

eng-runtime-lee: preliminary hypothesis: combination of larger KV footprint from canary + continuous batching increase creating larger in-flight messages -> head-of-line stalls on multiplexed socket paths. The runtime kernel selector picks a more aggressive kernel for canary that trades off latency variance for throughput. In canary we didn't simulate realistic APAC request shapes.

product-ryan: action item: add APAC-shaped workload to canary test harness and run with continuous batching on prior to future canary pushes.

support-nina: I'll reach out to affected customers with timeline and mitigation note.

oncall-amar: who owns the rollback artifact if we need to do full rollback to v1.3.5? Lee? Jordan?

eng-runtime-lee: I'll package v1.3.5 artifact and keep it ready for rollforward/rollback. prefer rollback only if we see recurrence after reintroducing.

incident-bot: Update: canary traffic in prod-apac 0% at 4309123510; mux local-only policy applied; active alerts suppressed.

eng-runtime-lee: capturing more perf dumps now. saving `heap.prof` and `kv-sizes.csv` under s3://redwood-ops/incident/4309123456/.

infra-tim: note for postmortem: check kernel patch list on apac fleet nodes and reconcile with eu/us fleets; also check epoll wakeup tuning flags.

oncall-amar: ok team — monitoring for 20m then will handoff to follow-on shift. Nina, include customer notes. Lee and Tim, please attach all artifacts to the incident ticket. Jordan, keep routers pinned until we confirm.

support-nina: will create customer follow-up thread and close once postmortem is scheduled.

product-ryan: good catch. add a task to product backlog: "APAC workload in canary harness + continuous batching smoke tests".

eng-runtime-lee: final note — when reintroducing canary, try: smaller batch target, disable aggressive kernel selector, and test with simulated long-context sessions.

oncall-amar: handoff: I'll tag this for oncall-shift-B at 4309124899. Next oncall please take over monitoring and coordinate any rollback if p99 creeps above 1.5s.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: from oncall-amar to oncall-bob at 4309124899.

sre-jordan: leaving the thread but will stay reachable. ping for router changes.

eng-runtime-lee: uploading artifacts now.

support-nina: customers notified.

oncall-amar: thanks all. creating follow-up postmortem stub with initial timeline + TL;DR mitigation steps.

incident-bot: Thread closed for live mitigation. Follow-up postmortem required.
